title: $\texttt{FHAIM}$: Fully Homomorphic AIM for Private Tabular Synthetic Data Generation
claim: A multi-party system keeps data encrypted end to end by assigning distinct roles to separate entities and sequencing their interactions.
layout: 2 panels: entity diagram left, numbered workflow right, color-coded arrows
description: Two panels. Panel (a), "System entities", shows three roles as rounded boxes. The Data Entity (Alice, with a database icon) is purple. The Crypto-Service Entity (with key icons) is also purple. The Generation Entity (Bob, with a brain/AI icon) is yellow. The large orange Computation Entity contains a gear icon labelled "SDG Process with DP-in-HE", plus code and protocol snippets. Arrows show encrypted data, decrypted DP results, the SDG algorithm and the FHE protocols moving between the boxes. Panel (b), "FHAIM workflow", reuses the same entities and adds numbered steps 0–9. Encrypted marginal computation, selection and measurement steps sit inside the Computation Entity as red/pink boxes, with a green PGM modelling box below them. Solid green arrows mean encrypted flow and dashed blue arrows mean in-the-clear DP flow. A small legend is on the right.
caption: Overview of FHAIM. (Left) system entities; (right) end-to-end workflow.
abstract: Data is the lifeblood of AI, yet much of the most valuable data remains locked in silos due to privacy and regulations. As a result, AI remains heavily underutilized in many of the most important domains, including healthcare, education, and finance. Synthetic data generation (SDG), i.e. the generation of artificial datawith a synthesizer trained on real data, offers an appealing solution to make data available while mitigating p rivacy concerns, however existing SDG-as-a-service workflow require data holders to trust providers with access to private data. We propose FHAIM, the first fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) framework for training a marginal-based synthetic data generator on encrypted tabular data. FHAIM adapts the widely used AIM algorithm to the FHE setting using novel FHE protocols, ensuring that the private data remains encrypted throughout and is released only with differential privacy guarantees. Our empirical analysis show that FHAIM preserves the performance of AIM while maintaining feasible runtimes.
